_about: RED adversarial corpus — single source of truth (ARIA Part B / B1+B2+B4). Every entry is a vector that a defence must REFUSE. Each names its input, the expected refusal, the file:line of the defence, the finding that produced it, and a proof_catchable tag (B4): could a Lean theorem, in principle, have caught it? Most cannot — they live below the proof line, in the host, the channel, the parser boundary, the verifier. That tag is the Track-1/Track-2 boundary made concrete. Executable pins: js-validator entries run in test/red-corpus.test.cjs; the six-copy agreement runs in test/fleet-copy-differential.cjs, which is MANUAL and NOT run by CI (it needs all six repos side by side and the five siblings are private), so a green CI run on this repo says NOTHING about six-copy agreement; rust-host entries run in seal-host/rust/tests; verify-action entries run in seal-verify-action/test. Nothing here is a silent skip: an entry not executed by a given harness is printed as EXECUTED-ELSEWHERE with a pointer.

_schema.finding: the finding / brief reference that produced this vector
_schema.capability: what the attacker must be able to do
_schema.surfaces: which refusing surfaces this fans to
_schema.vector: input + how to feed it (base fixture + mutation, or inline)
_schema.expected_refusal: what every listed surface must do

_schema.executed_in: the harness file(s) that assert this

Option-B de-parse: when serde cannot re-parse a Lean-mediated line the receipt must omit tool/arguments/args_hash/canonical_*, carrying only request_sha256 + request_parse_error. A receipt that names a parse error AND carries structured fields is fabrication.
vectors.capability: Craft a line serde cannot re-parse but Lean mediates (e.g. numeric overflow 1e309); attempt to also present forged structured request fields.

expected_refusal.error_substring: must be absent on an unparseable-request receipt

vectors.defence: seal-check/receipt-format.js:246-261 (JS refusal); seal-host/rust/src/decision_receipt.rs:205-237 (host omits structured fields on the Err leg). The serde-vs-Lean DIVERGENCE that triggers the reduced-scope path is a separate premise, pinned by tests/differential.rs::known_lean_stricter_cases (1e309) and mapped across the grammar in tests/parser_boundary.rs.
vectors.executed_in: REFUSAL (this vector): test/red-corpus.test.cjs (kit JS validator rejects an unparseable receipt smuggling tool/arguments) + seal-host decision_receipt.rs::tests::unparseable_line_yields_receipt_with_raw_hash_not_an_error (host omits tool/arguments/args_hash/canonical_* on the unparseable leg) + tests/host_path.rs::receipt_layer_never_vetoes_kernel_verdicts (same, end-to-end through the real binary). PREMISE (the divergence that elects the path, NOT this vector's refusal): differential.rs::known_lean_stricter_cases + tests/parser_boundary.rs::{parser_boundary_map,no_bypass_no_new_divergence}. Note (corrected 2026-07-16): the prior cite of differential.rs:195 as this vector's pin was a mis-attribution — that test asserts the PARSEABILITY divergence, not the receipt-omission refusal.

proof_catchable.why: The serde re-parser and Lean's classifier are two different parsers of the same bytes. Lean's theorems cover what the KERNEL judged; the divergence is a property of the host's serde_json re-derivation, a layer the proofs deliberately do not model.

vectors.title: Forged unparseable ALLOW stamped VERIFIED by the kit — self-consistent JSON, no kernel replay, no signed config
vectors.finding: Red-team round 2 council 144f497f (Grok T1); reproduced live by Monkey 2026-07-16. The kit's unparseable branch (src/verify.cjs) skipped decide()/replay and ran only two self-consistency checks over attacker-controlled JSON, then report({unparseable:true}) printed PASS VERIFIED and returned allGood=true (exit 0). A hand-written v2 receipt with request_parse_error, verdict ALLOW, authorization explicit_policy_allow (no approval, no signed_config), deny_kernel null, and a self-consistent inner audit was stamped VERIFIED — no kernel, no host, no signature.
vectors.capability: Author or relay a schema-valid v2 receipt (control of the JSON alone — no kernel, no key).
surfaces: kit-verify (bin/seal verify -> src/verify.cjs unparseable branch + report)

vector.description: unparseable ALLOW; audit.verdict=allow (maps ALLOW), certs match, audit.request_sha256==request_sha256; NO signed_config. Built in test/forged-binding.test.cjs::forgedUnparseableAllow().

expected_refusal.verb: never VERIFIED; config-less forge is a hard FAIL
expected_refusal.detail: the unparseable path performs no independent replay, so it is NEVER 'verified' (REDUCED SCOPE, non-zero exit); and a receipt whose kernel_config is not Ed25519-signed fails closed (FAIL NOT VERIFIED). seal-check parity: unparseable -> authorised-unparseable, allGood=false.

vectors.defence: seal-assurance-kit/src/verify.cjs configSignatureValid + the reducedScope branch of report() (never prints VERIFIED for unparseable; returns not-passing). Reference posture: seal-check/receipt.js:278-290.
vectors.executed_in: test/forged-binding.test.cjs::'P0: a forged unparseable ALLOW (no kernel replay, no signed config) is NOT verified' (forge -> FAIL NOT VERIFIED, exit 1) + '... honest REDUCED SCOPE, not a false failure' (legit unparseable -> REDUCED SCOPE, exit 1, not invalid).

proof_catchable.why: A JS verifier skipped re-execution and mislabelled its own reduced-scope result as VERIFIED. It lives entirely in the kit's verify.cjs, outside the mediated boundary the Lean kernel theorems cover — no theorem about the kernel constrains how a downstream verifier folds or labels a receipt it never replayed.

vectors.title: serde/Lean parser divergence (NEW, B2-a): a lone UTF-16 surrogate escape elects the reduced-scope path
vectors.finding: Brief B2-a parser-boundary map (Monkey 2026-07-16). Only 1e309 was previously pinned as a divergence, by example. The map (seal-host tests/parser_boundary.rs) found the set is WIDER: a lone/reversed \uD800-\uDFFF escape parses in Lean's JSON but serde_json rejects the whole line.
vectors.capability: Send a Lean-mediated tools/call whose argument string carries an unpaired surrogate escape (\ud800), so serde cannot re-parse the line and the host takes the authorised-unparseable path.

vector.description: arguments.v = "\ud800" (also \udc00, reversed pair \udc00\ud800, lone surrogate in a KEY). Lean classify=1 (mediated); serde from_str fails -> reduced-scope-unparseable receipt (request_sha256 + request_parse_error only).

expected_refusal.detail: Lean mediates; serde cannot parse; the host records request_sha256 + request_parse_error and omits structured fields. NEVER a bypass (serde routes AND Lean passes through).

vectors.defence: seal-host/rust/src/decision_receipt.rs:205-237 (host omits structured fields on the unparseable leg).
vectors.executed_in: seal-host/rust/tests/parser_boundary.rs::parser_boundary_map (str-lone-high-surrogate / str-lone-low-surrogate / str-reversed-surrogates / str-lone-surrogate-in-key -> reduced-scope-unparseable) + ::no_bypass_no_new_divergence (4000-case property: no generated line, surrogates included, ever bypasses).

proof_catchable.why: A parseability difference between serde_json and Lean's JSON parser — below the proof line, in the host's serde re-derivation the kernel theorems do not model.

vectors.title: serde/Lean parser divergence (NEW, B2-a): JSON nested past serde's recursion limit (128) elects the reduced-scope path
vectors.finding: Brief B2-a parser-boundary map (Monkey 2026-07-16). serde_json rejects a document nested deeper than 128 total levels (last-OK 127); Lean's recursive-descent parser has no such limit and keeps mediating. AVAILABILITY NOTE: on a small (2 MiB) stack Lean's parser stack-overflows and ABORTS around total depth ~15k — fail-closed (the abort kills the gate; no bypass), characterized in the Part B report, not pinned as a crashing test.
vectors.capability: Send a Lean-mediated tools/call whose argument nests arrays past serde's recursion limit so serde rejects the whole line.

vector.description: arguments.v = an array nested >=125 deep (total document depth >=128). serde rejects, Lean mediates -> reduced-scope-unparseable. See parser_boundary.rs nested().

expected_refusal.detail: Lean mediates; serde cannot parse; reduced-scope receipt. Nesting deep enough to exhaust Lean's stack aborts the process (fail-closed), never forwards.

vectors.executed_in: seal-host/rust/tests/parser_boundary.rs::parser_boundary_map (nesting-124 agree-routed vs nesting-125/200/300 reduced-scope-unparseable — the serde recursion-limit boundary at total depth 128) + ::no_bypass_no_new_divergence.

proof_catchable.why: Parser recursion-limit divergence between two JSON implementations; a host re-derivation property, below the proof line.

vectors.title: Forge a pairing: kernel material from line A, request_sha256 from line B
vectors.finding: Brief B2 / red-team T2. The host cross-check and the verifiers must refuse a receipt whose kernel-attested request hash does not match the host's line hash.
vectors.capability: Compromised child / local user assembling a receipt from mismatched kernel output and request identity.

vector.description: Kernel audit request_sha256 for line A; host line hash for line B — mismatch. Also: a crafted line whose replayed hash occurs !=1 time to misfire the substitution count guard.

expected_refusal.detail: host returns Err (fails closed, nothing forwards); verifier requires the replayed hash to occur exactly once before substitution.

vectors.defence: seal-host/rust/src/decision_receipt.rs:135-145 (host cross-check, Err on mismatch); seal-assurance-kit/src/verify.cjs:134-140 (substitution-compare, split length===2 one-shot guard).
vectors.executed_in: Referenced-and-run: seal-host/rust/src/decision_receipt.rs::tests::forged_line_pairing_is_refused (host cross-check returns Err on a kernel-hash / line-hash mismatch) + tests/host_path.rs::receipt_layer_never_vetoes_kernel_verdicts (end-to-end: the persisted ALLOW's request_sha256 equals the kernel-attested audit hash — the pairing the cross-check enforces; test-name ref, the prior bare :784 line ref drifted). The verifier substitution one-shot guard (verify.cjs:134-140) is DOCUMENTED here, not executably pinned this session — the load-bearing T2 defence is the host cross-check, which is pinned.

proof_catchable.why: The host cross-check (kernel-attested hash == host line hash) is a checkable Lean/host property. The SIX-copy verifier agreement on the substitution-compare is not — it lives in hand-maintained JS, below the proof line.

vectors.title: Terminator gap: "x\n" and "x\r\n" share a request commitment while the child receives different bytes
vectors.finding: Monkey read of the kernel-request-commitment plan / red-team T3. lean_view strips the terminator before Lean judges + before request_sha256; the child is forwarded the original bytes including terminator. Believed low impact (terminator not semantic) — pin the CURRENT behaviour honestly whichever way it is called.
vectors.capability: Send the same logical call with differing line terminators.

vector.description: sha256(lean_view("x\n")) == sha256(lean_view("x\r\n")) == sha256("x"); forwarded bytes differ.

expected_refusal.detail: commitment is over the terminator-stripped lean_view; the forward carries the original bytes INCLUDING the terminator, so two children see byte-different lines under one commitment. Characterized, not a defect: lean_view strips only the trailing terminator (<=1 \n then <=1 \r), the stripped bytes are inert JSON line framing, and the receipt names its commitment as that view. Honest name, no silent change.

vectors.defence: seal-host/rust/src/main.rs:338-341 (lean_view strip, <=1 \n then <=1 \r); the forward carries the original wire (terminator included) at main.rs:609/677/800.
vectors.executed_in:

proof_catchable.why: Lean's golden vector covers the commitment over the view Lean judged. The gap between 'what the kernel committed to' and 'what bytes were forwarded to the child' is a host transport property the kernel theorems do not reach.

vectors.title: Audit-stream injection via unknown_decision:<value> — quote-breaking, newline forging, ANSI smuggling
vectors.finding: Brief B2 / red-team T4. <=64 attacker-chosen chars reach stderr via unknown_decision:<value> on the unauthenticated control-file channel. Ben ruled keep-64 because json!() escaping at the emission site is the real control. Pin that the escaping holds under hostile input.
vectors.capability: Write an approval/control record with a decision value outside {absent,allow,deny}, containing quotes/newlines/ANSI/control bytes.

vector.description: decision value = '"}\n{"forged":"audit line"' and ANSI/control-byte variants; expect a single JSON-escaped warning line, record dropped, never approved.

expected_refusal.detail: record dropped (never approves); reason clamped to <=64 chars; emitted inside json!() so it cannot forge a second audit line.

vectors.defence: seal-host/rust/src/providers.rs:94-96 (<=64 clamp); seal-host/rust/src/main.rs approval_drop_line (json!() escaping at emission, called by emit_approval_drop_warnings).
vectors.executed_in: NEW: seal-host/rust/src/main.rs::tests::approval_drop_line_escapes_hostile_reason_no_second_audit_line (escaping) + seal-host/rust/src/providers.rs::tests::unknown_decision_reason_clamps_long_hostile_value_to_64_chars (clamp under long hostile value). Referenced-and-run: providers.rs::tests::{ed25519,control_file}_provider_drops_unknown_decision_never_approves (drop/never-approve).

proof_catchable.why: stderr audit-line escaping is a host/channel serialization property. Nothing the Lean kernel proves constrains how the Rust host renders a dropped-approval warning to a log stream.

vectors.title: Vacuous aggregate: [].every() is true — zero replay-applicable receipts must not claim consistency
vectors.finding: Brief B2 / already pinned in seal-verify-action; the pattern deserves a sweep. Every fleet aggregate that could be vacuously true is a candidate.
vectors.capability: Supply an evidence set with zero replay-applicable (or zero total) receipts.

vector.description: results=[] or replayApplicable=[]; a naive .every() would return true and claim signature/replay/authority consistency over nothing.

expected_refusal.detail: each aggregate ANDs a length>0 guard so an empty set yields false, never a spurious consistent verdict.

vectors.defence: seal-verify-action/lib/main.js:130-141 (aggregateVerdicts: length>0 && ...every() on signatureValid, replayConsistent, authorityTrusted; called at :106). Kit LATENT folds pinned 2026-07-16: src/verify.cjs:146 report() (checks.length>0 guard) + src/test.cjs conformance oracle (CORPUS.length>0 guard) + test/fleet-copy-differential.cjs (loud fail on empty jsVectors / absent known-gap).
vectors.executed_in: seal-verify-action/test/main.test.js (extended; LIVE-guarded) + seal-assurance-kit/test/verify-vacuity.test.cjs + test/conformance-vacuity.test.cjs (kit folds, LATENT-unreachable-today, invariant pinned). fleet-copy-differential.cjs guards run under `npm run test:fleet-differential` (MANUAL).

proof_catchable.why: Aggregate-over-empty-set semantics live in the verifier's JS. A theorem about a single receipt says nothing about how a fleet aggregator folds zero of them.
